text:
Ryan O'Reilly's season is a reminder that the 2019 Conn Smythe winner never needed to be loud to matter. He has 17 points in 19 games, nine on the power play, while centering big minutes for a Nashville team that has won six straight. Seven goals on 5.5 expected is a bit kind, and a 22.6% shooting rate is likely to drift down, but nothing about his start looks like a mirage.

The quieter numbers tell you who he is. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 93rd percentile among forwards: when he has the puck in the offensive zone, the next shot is often a teammate's. NHL EDGE has his top skating speed at 23.1 mph, 94th percentile, which is not what you picture from a 35-year-old two-way center. The thing worth watching: he has gone three games without a point and hasn't shot much lately, with no shots in four of his last eight. At five-on-five Nashville takes 47% of the expected goals with him on, close to its level without him.
headline: Ryan O'Reilly, still the quiet center who matters
